title: Process versus outcome supervision
bottleneck: Supervising only outcomes rewards models for reaching correct answers via flawed or deceptive reasoning, while supervising the process requires step-level labels that are expensive and themselves gameable. Outcome supervision trains models to be right for the wrong reasons; process supervision doesn't scale to tasks where humans can't verify intermediate steps. The field hasn't resolved which to use where. Hybrid schemes exist but inherit both failure modes: expensive labels that still reward surface-plausible reasoning.
why_it_blocks: The choice shapes what models actually learn. Wrong supervision targets produce capable systems with alien, unverifiable internal reasoning. Mis-set supervision targets are invisible in training metrics and surface only as deployment surprises.
current_state: Process-supervision work on math shows promise in narrow domains. General methods for process supervision of open-ended reasoning don't exist.
